LESSON: SELF-AWARENESS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Creation
Topic 1.1: Self-awareness

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Self-awareness. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why are you a special creation?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. recognise his or her uniqueness as a creation of God
2. appreciate his or her uniqueness as God’s special creation

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SELF-AWARENESS
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Self-awareness helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: SELF-AWARENESS
Study Self-awareness like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Recognise his or her uniqueness as a creation of God

What this means
In this part you learn to recognise his or her uniqueness as a creation of God. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognise his or her uniqueness as a creation of God.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Self-awareness” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognise his or her uniqueness as a creation of God. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate his or her uniqueness as God’s special creation

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate his or her uniqueness as God’s special creation. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate his or her uniqueness as God’s special creation.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Self-awareness in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate his or her uniqueness as God’s special creation. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Self-awareness is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Self-awareness” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: recognise his or her uniqueness as a creation of God)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Self-awareness in your own words. (skill: appreciate his or her uniqueness as God’s special creation)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Self-awareness to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: recognise his or her uniqueness as a creation of God.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate his or her uniqueness as God’s special creation.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Self-awareness from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Self-awareness: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Self-awareness?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why are you a special creation?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Self-awareness means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: recognise his or her uniqueness as a creation of God.
5. Be able to: appreciate his or her uniqueness as God’s special creation.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
